summary: Dashboard snapshot UUID rotation after retention prune causes orphaned alert attachments
description: Issue summary: After a scheduled retention prune run completed in prod (us-east), several dashboard alert history entries reference snapshot UUIDs that no longer exist in the metrics index. Those alerts retain attachments (console snapshots / links to traces) but the underlying snapshot UUIDs were rotated or removed by the prune job, causing alert pages to render an empty attachment list and any alert-to-trace anchor links to 404. Impact: Customer-facing alert history shows missing screenshots/attachments for recurring incidents for the last 30 days. This prevents GardenBooks SREs from investigating historical context for alerts and breaks runbook linkages. Environment: prod/us-east (primary), affected customers in eu-west via mirror. Retention/compaction job id: retention-prune-2026-03-09-22:00 (kafka partition reindex coincided).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to GardenBooks org in Console (prod, us-east). 2) Open Alerts > Alert History for rule 'api-latency-slo-breach' (alert id: A-2026-GB-1192). 3) Click on an alert occurrence dated between 2026-02-10 and 2026-03-09. 4) Attempt to open attached dashboard snapshot or 'View linked trace'. 5) Observe UI shows 'Attachment not found' and trace link returns 404 or points to a rotated snapshot UUID. Expected behavior: Alert attachments and trace anchors should remain resolvable for full retention window and alert detail pages should gracefully show historical artifacts. Actual behavior: Attachments missing, alert timeline shows attachment count but clicking yields not found. Logs/observations: - retention-prune service logs show prune of 'snapshot-index-v3' shards at 2026-03-09T22:12Z. - Sample missing snapshot UUIDs: snap-7f4b2d3a, snap-7f4b2d3b. - Console API returned 404 for GET /api/v1/snapshots/snap-7f4b2d3a (request-id: req-0a9bce). - Alert UI still lists attachment: 1 (but underlying store returns empty).

investigation_notes: Initial triage: retention-prune job removed snapshot docs that were only referenced by alert history entries. Alert history references are not treated as a strong dependency during compaction. We identified ~42 alert occurrences across GardenBooks org with orphaned snapshot UUIDs. Root cause hypothesis: migration to snapshot-index-v3 introduced a UUID rotation mapping that was not propagated to alert history; compaction pruned the old docs. We confirmed s3 cold-backup contains original snapshot tarballs for many UUIDs. Immediate mitigation: stop further prune cycles for snapshot-index-v3 until retention config is patched. Longer-term: add transactional pinning or a GC guard for any object referenced by alert_history index.
resolution_notes: TBD - patch in progress. Planned actions: (a) patch console UI to surface 'snapshot removed by retention' with trace links where available, (b) run backfill job to restore metadata for high-impact UUIDs from cold backup and rehydrate the snapshot index, (c) change retention-prune to consult alert_history references before deletion, and (d) add a postmortem and follow-up engineering tasks (INT ticket to update retention policy).
